text: The exact credited-day formula for the 1994 strike and the 144-game 1995 season was not read. Working rule: championship-season days on the calendar only, then the ordinary cap. No strike buy-back is applied.
No 2022 side letter adding service on top of the restored 162-game season was found. Working rule: ordinary counting on the calendar window, with no proration.

Whether the 2021 season used a 15-day or a 10-day floor for pitcher injured-list stints and pitcher options is unresolved (2020 announcement and the 2021 rules versus a glossary note that says the 15-day pitcher list returned in 2022). Working rule: any major-league injured list counts, whatever the length printed on the row. The recall date in the feed is used as written; the minimum stay is not re-imposed.

Attachment 2 denies Opening Day credit for a pre-roster-deadline option, outright, or DFA of a player who was already optioned. A DFA of a player who was on the major-league roster, still open on Opening Day, is not named in that sentence. Working rule, matching the instruction for this job: no preseason DFA earns Opening Day, whether or not he was optioned. Official totals for a few such players would settle the narrower case.

The glossary says a drug suspension reduced by 20 or more games under the mitigation provision can still earn service. That sentence was not read in the drug program itself. Working rule: a drug suspension earns service only when the exceptions file says so. Mitigation is not inferred.

A five-optional-assignment cap per season is in the public 2022 recap and the glossary, and was not found as a numeral in the agreement text during the research pass. It does not change how a given option day counts. Working rule: the cap is not enforced.

The 2026 cutoff 2.133 is the official figure. Cutoffs for 2012-2017, 2019, and 2020 in the reference file rest on later recap lists, not a standalone article re-read for this job. Those rows were already in the file and were not changed.

The 2020 scale is days times the original schedule length divided by the revised schedule length. The official denominator was not read from the signed March 2020 agreement. Working rule: the denominator is this calendar's championship-season length. A player on the roster or the major-league injured list the whole season reaches the cap either way.

Service is written for up to two years of active duty and up to thirty days of National Guard emergency duty. The feed does not say which kind of duty a military-list row is. Working rule: a major-league military-list placement counts, and spells are not trimmed at those caps.
The designation window before 2012 was not established. Working rule: the 2012-16 length is the safety cap. See accrual.dfa-window-pre2012.

The 2022-26 text ends service on the last regularly scheduled game and does not mention tiebreakers. An earlier text, quoted in public reporting, credited a tiebreaker day. The 2017-21 book was not re-read. Working rule: through 2021 a tiebreaker counts for the clubs that played it; from 2022 it does not.

The option date does not count if the option was after the start of a major-league game he could have played, and the recall date does count if the recall was after the start of a minor-league game. The feed has dates only. Those two exceptions are not applied.
